## The two failures

### 1. `emojipicker TestFuzzy_OutOfOrderQueryMatchesNothing`

```
fuzzy_test.go:110: query "krt" matched [bookmark_tabs]; subsequence matching is
                   IN-ORDER (G10) so nothing here should match
```

Subsequence matching must be **in-order**: every rune of the query appears in the
name, in sequence. `rkt` matches `rocket` (r-o-**c**-**k**-e-**t** — r, k, t in
order). `krt` must match nothing, because `k` precedes `r` in the query but not in
any candidate.

`bookmark_tabs` matching `krt` means the tier predicate and the score function
disagree about what "subsequence" means — likely because one of them folds,
squashes `_`, or strips skin tones, producing a different rune stream than the
other assumed. Find the divergence; do not just add a length guard.

The reference implementation this was extracted from is the original
`channelfinder` matcher: its `subsequenceScore` doc says "every rune of q appears
in name in order". `git log` and `git show` on `internal/ui/channelfinder/model.go`
will show you the pre-extraction version.

### 2. `reactionpicker TestFuzzyReaction_FrecentOutranksPrefixMatch`

```
fuzzy_test.go:144: frecent entry matching the query is not in the results;
    filtered = [aaa_frec fortune_cookie four_leaf_clover firecracker ...]
```

The frecent ("recently used") entry that matches the query is absent from the
results **entirely** — not merely mis-ranked. That is the signature of the recent
tier being applied as a FILTER over an already-capped candidate set, rather than
as a ranking tier over all matches. Check the order of operations: if the cap
(`MaxVisible` in emojipicker, 50 in reactionpicker) is applied BEFORE ranking,
a higher tier becomes unreachable.

Required ranking, per plan item `fuzzy-emoji`: **recent (frecent) > prefix >
substring > subsequence**, case/accent-folded via `text.Fold`, preserving the
`MaxVisible` cap and input-order stability within a tier.

Note `frecent_emoji` is GLOBAL with no team column (`internal/cache/db.go:151-156`).
So "recent" means *matching entries ∩ frecent* — never inject a frecent name that
is not itself a match for the query, and skip frecent names that no longer exist.

## Ranking must be a total order

With 4 tiers + a score + a tie-break + a cap, two entries can compare equal and
the output then depends on map iteration order or a non-stable sort. That is a
golden-test flake generator. Use `sort.SliceStable`, never iterate a Go map in the
ranking path, and make sure "input-order stability within a tier" is actually
guaranteed rather than incidental.

## Do not break the other consumers

`internal/fuzzy` is shared by FOUR consumers. `channelfinder` and `mentionpicker`
expectations must NOT change — the plan is explicit about it, and the gate's P2P
set runs both suites on every invocation. A silent ranking change in the channel
switcher that no test catches is the dangerous case; if you change scoring, check
what it does to those two.

`internal/ui/mode_reaction_picker_test.go` lives in `package ui` and asserts on
reactionpicker's ranking through the App. It is in the P2P set too. You may not
edit files in `internal/ui/` top-level — if that test needs to change, STOP and
say so.

## Repo conventions (`AGENTS.md` — read it, it is authoritative)

- Before writing any helper, search: case folding (`text.Fold`), display width
  (`emoji.Width`), shortcode mapping (`emoji.CodeMap`, `emoji.StripSkinTone`) all
  already exist. `AGENTS.md` has the tables. The repo's single worst recurring
  defect is re-implementing something that already exists.
- A tier constant, cap, or fold function must live in exactly ONE place. If the
  same threshold is defined in both `internal/fuzzy` and a consumer, DELETE one —
  never alias. Two spellings of one value silently change behaviour between call
  sites.
- Tests are stdlib `testing` only. No testify, no new dependencies — the gate
  fails if `go.mod`/`go.sum` change at all.
- `AGENTS.md` must list `internal/fuzzy` in its shared-helpers table; the plan
  requires that in the same commit as the extraction. Check whether it does, and
  add it if not. `AGENTS.md` is in the repo ROOT — editing it is allowed and
  expected, it is not another lane's file.

## Performance

The matcher runs per keystroke over ~3.9k emoji aliases plus channels plus
members. Avoid per-call re-folding of the whole corpus. Only optimize if you can
show a real interactive-latency cost — do not add a cache the tests cannot see.
